To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the majority of thyroid cancers are well differentiated and have an excellent prognosis, 2) thyroid cancers are often diagnosed incidentally and are often multifocal, and 3) there is no evidence to support routine total thyroidectomy for patients diagnosed with well-differentiated thyroid carcinoma.
the treatment of WDTC with surgery, radioiodine and TSH suppression is effective, with a low risk of recurrence and death.
the use of the term “well-differentiated” in the context of thyroid cancer is not supported by the current evidence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel, non-toxic, non-radioactive imaging probes for the detection of cancer.
the development of a novel, noninvasive, optical imaging method that can be used to monitor the treatment of well-differentiated thyroid cancer in a clinical setting.

the development of a new approach to the treatment of well-differentiated thyroid carcinoma (WDTC) that is based on the use of a novel therapeutic agent, a recombinant human thyroid-stimulating hormone (rhTSH) analog, that has been shown to be effective in stimulating thyroid hormone release from the tumor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the treatment of well-differentiated thyroid carcinoma is based on the following: (1) The primary treatment of choice is surgical removal of the tumor, including the central portion of the thyroid gland and all of the cervical lymph nodes, if any are palpable.

there is no evidence to suggest that the treatment of patients with differentiated thyroid cancer is not beneficial and that there is no justification for abandoning the current standard of care for patients with well-differentiated thyroid cancer.
the best treatment for well differentiated thyroid carcinoma is total thyroidectomy with a central neck dissection and radioactive iodine ablation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the thyroid gland is a glandular organ situated in the front part of the neck and it produces thyroid hormones, which are essential for the normal functioning of the body.
the treatment of thyroid cancer has evolved over time.

the treatment of patients with well-differentiated thyroid cancer (WDTC) should be tailored to the risk of recurrence, and the treatment of high-risk patients should be based on a multidisciplinary team approach.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can identify patients with differentiated thyroid cancer who are at high risk of recurrence.
there is an urgent need for a more effective treatment of thyroid cancer.
there is no single treatment that is best for all patients with differentiated thyroid cancer.
